reason: The pictures show fluid movement bending the sensor hairs, so I'll build the turning sensors first.
expectation: I expect the cells to fit into the loops and detect head turns as the fluid moves.

alternatives.reason: The weights and tilt cells also look like a clear pair, but I want to start with turning.

effect: The canals detect changes in turning, and their nerve bundle still needs connecting.
reaction: The fluid lag bending the sensors makes sense.
reason: I'll build the tilt sensors next; the picture shows the weights resting above their sensory cells.
expectation: I expect the weights to help the cells detect tilt as the jelly layer shifts.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the turning sensors to the balance nerves also seems useful, but I want to build both sensors first.

effect: The weighted layer bends the hairs during tilt or changes in straight-line movement; both sensor types are now built.
reaction: The shifting layer makes the weights' purpose clearer.
reason: I'll bring the two sensor types together before connecting their nerve routes.
expectation: I expect a combined balance-sensing structure containing both turning and tilt sensors.

alternatives.reason: I could connect the turning sensors to the nerves first, but I want to join the sensors together.

effect: The turning and weighted sensors are now together beside the hearing coil, with spaces for balance nerves.
reaction: It's useful to see how the balance organs fit beside the hearing structures.
reason: I'll connect the balance nerves to the organs so their sensor signals have a route toward the brain.
expectation: I expect the nerves to connect the balance sensors to the brain, though the outgoing muscle routes may still need joining.

alternatives.reason: Joining the incoming and outgoing routes also supports the goal, but I want to connect the sensors first.

effect: Both kinds of balance sensor now have nerve fibres leading toward the brain; the outgoing routes remain to be joined.
reaction: The shared incoming connection is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should connect the sensors to the eye and posture routes.
expectation: I expect a connected route from the balance organs through the brain toward the eye and posture muscles.

effect: The completed inner ear connects both balance sensors through the brain to eye and posture muscles; vision and signals from muscles and joints also help.
reaction: The picture of the eyes turning opposite the head makes the route feel useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the sensors to the eye and posture routes was most worthwhile because it showed how balance signals relate to something familiar: keeping your eyes on a point while turning your head.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the two sensor types felt less informative than building them; it mainly showed where they sit beside the hearing coil.

surprise.text: The weighted sensors also respond when straight-line movement changes, not just when the head tilts.

arbitrary.text: No action felt completely arbitrary, although joining the sensor types before connecting nerves was more about arranging parts than explaining a new function.

continue.text: I would probably continue: seeing the balance sensors connect to eye movement made me curious about how another body system fits together.
